candidates.exact_span:
a. The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this
      section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a mandatory toxicity-testing monitoring obligation; whether and when this obligation applies determines if monitoring was required for FY2025.
Scopes which discharge point the toxicity requirements bind; different outfall applicability changes which measurements, limits, and monitoring-evidence cases are in scope.

Sets the effluent-dilution threshold referenced in chronic lethal and sub-lethal failure definitions; a different critical-dilution value would change whether reported toxicity results constitute exceedance.

Specifies the dilution concentrations that must be tested to determine NOEC and compliance; different series interpretation changes both the applicable test protocol and whether results support a compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
TEST SPECIES AND METHODS           Ceriodaphnia dubia / Method 1002.0 (EPA-
                                    821-R-02-013 or latest version)
                                    Pimephales promelas/ Method 1000.0
                                    (EPA/821/R-02-013 or latest version)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which species and EPA methods are required for toxicity monitoring; interpretation of method version or species applicability changes which monitoring obligations were in force.

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defers sample-type requirements to PART I; without resolving that cross-reference, whether the correct sample type was required and whether reported or missing data satisfies the obligation remains uncertain.

candidates.exact_span:
b. The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest
      effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control
      (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the operative compliance metric for lethal toxicity; different interpretation of NOEC or the 95% confidence criterion changes whether a reported test result exceeds the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span:
Chronic lethal test failure is
      defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a
      test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the condition under which a lethal toxicity result constitutes noncompliance; interpretation of 'statistically significant' or 'at or below the critical dilution' changes exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span:
Chronic sub-lethal test failure is defined as a
      demonstration of a statistically significant sub-lethal effect (i.e., growth or reproduction)
      at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the condition under which a sub-lethal toxicity result constitutes noncompliance; different interpretation of sub-lethal effects or the critical-dilution linkage changes whether measurements exceed applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span:
c. This permit may be reopened to require WET limits, chemical specific effluent limits,
      additional testing, and/or other appropriate actions to address toxicity.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates WET numeric limits may not currently be in effect and could be imposed later; interpretation affects whether enforceable numeric discharge limits exist for toxicity versus report-only or protocol-based compliance.

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall repeat a test, including the control and all effluent dilutions, if the
      procedures and quality assurance requirements defined in the test methods or in this
      permit are not satisfied, including the following additional criteria:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes when a toxicity test must be repeated rather than accepted; whether QA failures occurred changes both ongoing monitoring obligations and whether available results constitute adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Sampling Requirement *             Minimum of 3 samples             Minimum of 3 samples
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a minimum sample count for toxicity testing; interpretation of whether three samples were required and obtained changes monitoring-obligation fulfillment and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Holding time *                     36 hours for first use           36 hours for first use
candidates.computation_change_reason: Limits allowable time before first use of a sample; exceeding holding time may invalidate results and trigger retest obligations or leave evidence unresolved.

candidates.exact_span:
Test Acceptability Criteria        ≥80% survival of all control     ≥80% survival of all control
                                    organisms.                       organisms.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when a toxicity test is unacceptable and must be repeated; whether control survival met this threshold changes if monitoring was satisfactorily completed and whether reported data are usable evidence.
